hints: Focus on the reagents and conditions for each numbered reaction, they each point to a different classic reaction type of alcohols.
Recall that hot Al2O3 causes dehydration, ethanoic acid with concentrated sulfuric acid causes esterification, and HBr causes substitution of OH by Br.
Check for H2O alongside the main organic product in each case, alkene plus water, ester plus water, and bromoalkane plus water, to find which combination is complete.
walkthrough:
**Identify reaction 1**

Great start, hot aluminium oxide is a dehydrating agent. It removes H and OH from adjacent carbons to form an alkene.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify reaction 2**

This is esterification. A warm alcohol plus a carboxylic acid with concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst forms an ester and water.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify reaction 3**

This is nucleophilic substitution. The OH group is replaced by Br from HBr, and the H from HBr joins the OH to make water.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Combine the conclusion**

All three reactions produce water as one product. So statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct. Reaction 1 gives propene + water, reaction 2 gives propyl ethanoate + water, and reaction 3 gives 1-bromopropane + water. All three have water as a product.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. Students choose this if they forget that substitution of an alcohol with HBr also forms water from the OH group plus H.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3. Students choose this if they think dehydration over hot Al2O3 gives only the alkene and miss the water eliminated.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. Students choose this if they recognise dehydration but confuse esterification as giving only ester, or substitution as giving only the bromoalkane.
